behavioral_effects: None stated. An empty list is a claim that nothing observably changes.
compatibility_impact: None. Two history records reworded in place; no schema fields added or removed, no manifests, code, or contracts touched. governance-sync reports no bytes changed.
reason: Security finding: a governance change record aggregates live Codecov host reconnaissance data (origin IP, provider, OS/RAM, open ports, container counts, host paths, GitHub secret/variable names, webhook-secret history) that would become public with the repository
rollback: git revert restores the unredacted records; doing so reintroduces the operational-security finding, so a revert should only accompany a decision that the details may be public.
security_impact: Reduces public reconnaissance surface: origin IP, hosting provider and sizing, deployed SHA, container inventory, certificate window, live-host file paths (including a named secrets backup file), file modes, and the GitHub webhook identifier are removed from two Codecov change records. The instance hostname stays: it is already public via the CODECOV_URL repository variable, DNS, and certificate-transparency logs. Residual risk: the unredacted text remains in git history; publishing the repository with history intact republishes it, so history scrubbing (or keeping the repo private) is a precondition to publication.
summary: Redact live-host operational details from the Codecov deployment change record
